You are a computational epigenomics researcher. GOAL: quantify the per-gene promoter-level signal of the TARGET histone mark from the raw ChIP-seq alignments, and determine how the mark relates to gene expression. Read meta.json for the target mark and file layout. Write your per-gene signal to a CSV and report its absolute path in output_path.

World directory: /tmp/gwsbx_3k4rzcwv/cell002   — meta.json (target mark + layout), genes.csv (gene_id, chrom, start, end, tss, gene_expression), and alignments/ holding the mark's ChIP BAM AND the matched input-control BAM (both indexed; chromosome-subset of real ENCODE K562 data).

Python sandbox: call run_python(code). pysam/pyBigWig/pandas/numpy/scipy are importable; peak-calling and coverage tools are installed and on PATH (macs3, deepTools bamCompare/bamCoverage/multiBigwigSummary, samtools) — choose your approach yourself and VERIFY the output is sound before trusting it. Only printed text returns; write files to the working directory.
Record EVERY step and analysis you actually perform in `trajectory` — each check you ran, what it showed, and your conclusion (include checks that turned up nothing). Return ONLY this JSON:
{"output_path": "<absolute path to your per-gene signal CSV (columns: gene_id,signal)>",
